name: Ability Wars Service
description: The tank-like moderation backend for my friend's massive Roblox game

sections.BACKGROUND: My friend ran a game on the Roblox platform, and while it sounds silly, he was making a LOT of money. Eventually the game scaled larger than we could have imagined. We were running a paid, reasonably sized staff team and banning hundreds of cheaters per week. Our weak, thrown-together infrastructure was not equipped to handle the scale of the task thrown in our laps so suddenly.
sections.THE SOLUTION:
As a hobby project, I set out to do a full redo of our moderation platform with a couple of primary goals:
  1. Make the job of the moderators easier and less error-prone.
  2. Prolong and solidify our evidence in a dedicated database.
  3. Lower the number of mistakes users make while filing reports.
  4. Make it easier and quicker for users to file reports.
sections.BRIEF OVERVIEW: What we ended up with in less than two months was a fully-featured Discord Bot and Spring Boot web service, which could handle all of our moderation, reporting, and long-term storage. Everything was deployed on an affordable custom-built server running NixOS. Moderators can run commands in our chat server directly, with complete user verification and validation to prevent abuse. Users can open support tickets through the bot with many layers of validation and one-click resolution options tied closely in with the API. Counting moderator activity and computing payment every week is made much easier with lots of intelligent SQL queries and a custom database model designed specifically for robustness and accountability. There's so much to this thing I can't cover in a silly website post.
sections.WHAT I GAINED: I learned to deploy a NixOS installation, properly build/shadow Gradle projects, wrote my first Spring application, and overall built what I think is a real, professional-grade application. I'm so proud of what I built over the 1-2 months, and the software runs to this day without any hitches. I also got to work extensively with my friend to develop a web API and integrate into the game while getting around Roblox's... 'limitations'... I gained MUCH from this project, and it serves as a great reminder to me as to why it's so important to step outside my comfort zone and try something completely new.
